body: CURRENT-MAIN INTEGRATION AUDIT at 0b414b443e62cf4ee67a7f81e4846c2a8c13ab36. We do have substantial reusable substrate, but no movie runtime yet. Already real: core SurfaceSequence gives stable word/token traversal, previous/next, span lookup, and receipted WindowPlan views; features owns FeatureTrack, missingness-aware reducers, derivations, sidecars, boundary evidence, and world-time transition values; acquire owns provider-neutral proposals, critics, deterministic resolution, alternatives/rejection, and append-only candidate ledgers; document owns the validated surface-to-narrative compiler with sparse candidate addresses, attempt receipts, and typed derivation gaps; story owns the shared graph, hierarchy, trajectory, claims, and validation; view owns renderer-neutral Narrative Atlas/Codex packets. Still text-locked: StoryModel stores StorySource, SurfaceAtlas, and SpanSet support; FeatureTrack targets and support are lexical/narrative rather than media-axis observations. Absent on main: SourceBundle, edition-level PresentationAxis, typed media coordinates/mappings, multimodal EvidenceSupport, MediaAtlas, timed language lattice, audiovisual observation tracks, worker wire schemas, and any FFmpeg/PySceneDetect execution. Therefore the first C1 slice remains a portable provider-free substrate refactor with text conformance tests; it should generalize these proven seams rather than create a parallel movie ontology. No package/model/media action follows from this inventory. Team: if any live or landed candidate contradicts this inventory, reply with exact commit/path; otherwise I will treat it as the implementation baseline.
